text:
morgan: Heads-up — saw a weird billing spike in canary last night. Investigating, but quick summary: resumed streaming sessions that had a KV prefix truncation ended up creating provisional charges for the same toolcall twice.
morgan: Minimal repro so far: client opens stream, we emit some tokens, toolcall triggers, then client reconnects -> resume attaches a shorter prefix (kv eviction) and we retry the toolcall path. Ledger ends up with provisional entries that both look valid.
kai: ugh. any trace ids or logs?
morgan: yes — grabbed a sample from 2026-03-19 22:41 UTC:
```
INFO resume session=ses_8f3 prefix_len=128 resumed_at=token_542 toolcall_id=tc_a1 provisional_charge=0.012
WARN toolcall-retry detected session=ses_8f3 toolcall_id=tc_a1 retry_reason=client_reconnect
INFO ledger append provisional id=prov_93 key=(session:ses_8f3, toolcall:tc_a1) amount=0.012
INFO ledger append provisional id=prov_94 key=(session:ses_8f3, toolcall:tc_a1) amount=0.012
```
morgan: You can see two provisonals with same session+toolcall, different provis ids.
sarah: are both provisional entries later confirmed? or does one get rolled back?
morgan: in that trace both eventually remained provisional for ~7 minutes until auto-commit window closed; then a reconciler deduped one but the console shows a transient +0.024 spike in token usage which alarmed SRE.
tom: So two questions: why are both created, and why doesn't the dedupe happen earlier? Could be race between resume flow and retry path.
kai: My hunch: resume route reconstructs a toolcall checksum from prefix tokens. If kv truncation shortens prefix, the checksum differs, so the router thinks it's a different invocation and issues another provisional charge. Then later the offline reconciler uses more complete traces and dedupes by actual toolcall payload and confirmed intent.
sarah: That maps to a hypothesis I had — we use different keying for provisional ledger writes vs final dedupe. Provisional uses (session, toolcall-checksum-v1) and reconciler uses payload-hash-v2 that collapses them.
opsbot: Incident 2026-03-19-22:40 — provisional-double-charge detected in canary. Pager muted.
kai: Ok if that's right, fix options:
- Make provisional keying stronger: include deterministic toolcall-id header from client (requires client change)
- Use session+toolcall-canonicalized-payload for provisional writes (compute canonical during streaming resume)
- Add short-lived dedupe window in router that checks recent provis for same session and similar payload (>90% sim)
- Change console UX to show provisional vs confirmed and mark transient spikes
morgan: I prefer option 2 for correctness, fallback to 3 for quick mitigation. Option 1 is ideal but not fast.
tom: Are there perf implications computing canonicalized payload during streaming? We do incremental hashes already for prefix caching.
kai: Incremental rolling hash should be cheap if we reuse KV prefix digest. The tricky part is what "canonicalize" means for toolcall args (we have nested JSON, sometimes order differs).
sarah: We already canonicalize prompt embeddings for cached lookups (stable sort keys). Reuse that util.
morgan: For short-term mitigation, can we add router check: if session has recent provisional for same toolcall_id (or similar payload) within 30s, skip writing duplicate provisional and attach trace to existing one?
kai: Yes — implement a soft dedupe map in the router (LRU per session) keyed by (toolcall-signature) with TTL 30s. If match, annotate and short-circuit ledger write. Should reduce spikes immediately.
tom: Dashboard request: can the console show both provisional and confirmed columns in the per-route cost table? Ops wants to see provisional drift.
sarah: I can add a small panel: per-route provisional vs confirmed tokens over last 1h, with a filter for canary tag.
morgan: Great. Also add an eval/alert: if provisional > confirmed by > 10% sustained for 5min -> page the SRE rotation.
kai: I'll own the router soft-dedupe quick fix. Plan:
- PR: soft dedupe LRU map + unit tests (by EOD)
- Add debug logs to emit prov_id on dedupe path
- Short-term console patch: sarah to add panel (next sprint)
- Longer-term: refactor provisional keying to use canonicalized toolcall payload (follow-up ticket: #INFR-1427)
morgan: Assigning ticket INFR-1427 to kai for investigation, create INFR-1428 for console panel.
billing-bot: Billing reconciliation job flagged 2 canary sessions: session=ses_8f3, ses_c21. Suspicious delta=0.024 tokens each.
kai: Repro steps I need from anyone with a reliable client: sequence of events that triggers kv eviction during an in-flight toolcall. If anyone has that, ping me.
morgan: I'll paste a synthetic client trace I used in the repro channel.
sarah: One more UX note — when console shows provisional spikes, include a link to the ledger entries and trace id. That made debugging way faster last time.
tom: ack. thanks all. I'll monitor canary after kai's patch.
morgan: Thanks — will update this thread when PR is up.
